SEARCH
Package neqsim.process.processmodel

Class ProcessModel

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.processmodel.ProcessModel
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Runnable
public class ProcessModel extends Object implements Runnable, Serializable
ProcessModel class. Manages a collection of processes that can be run in steps or continuously.

This class supports serialization via saveToNeqsim(String) and loadFromNeqsim(String) for full model persistence.

Version:
1.0
Author:
ESOL

    • DEFAULT_ENGINEERING_TOLERANCE

      public static final double DEFAULT_ENGINEERING_TOLERANCE
      Relative tolerance the auto-tuner applies when no tolerance was set explicitly. 1e-3 (0.1 %) is an engineering-grade accuracy for process calculations: it is well below plant instrument and EOS uncertainty, yet loose enough that recycle-rich plants converge in a fraction of the passes a 1e-4 gate needs.

    • DEFAULT_MASS_CLOSURE_TOLERANCE

      public static final double DEFAULT_MASS_CLOSURE_TOLERANCE
      Plant mass-closure error the auto-tuner accepts, as a fraction of plant feed (0.1 %).

      The boundary residual only measures how much stream values still move between outer passes. It is blind to an unconverged Recycle, whose open tear is a standing mass source or sink: the plant can sit perfectly still on the boundary metric while destroying several percent of the feed. This gate adds the missing physical criterion.

      See Also:

    • unitMassClosureGate

      private boolean unitMassClosureGate
      Whether the unit-level closure figure also blocks a converged verdict.

      Off by default: a non-recycle unit that does not conserve mass is an equipment defect rather than something the outer solver can close, so gating on it would iterate to the cap and bury the real diagnosis. The figure is always reported so the defect is never silent.

      true if optimized execution is enabled

      public void setUseOptimizedExecution(boolean useOptimizedExecution)
      Enable or disable optimized execution for individual ProcessSystems.

      When enabled (default), each ProcessSystem uses ProcessSystem.runOptimized() which auto-selects the best execution strategy (parallel for feed-forward, hybrid for recycle processes). When disabled, uses standard sequential SimulationInterface.run().

      Parameters:

    • setPreventNestedParallelExecution

      public void setPreventNestedParallelExecution(boolean preventNestedParallelExecution)
      Enable or disable nested parallel execution prevention.

      When enabled, areas that run concurrently at the ProcessModel level temporarily execute their child ProcessSystems in sequential mode. This keeps area-level workers from blocking while also submitting inner unit-operation work to the same shared thread pool.

      Parameters:
      preventNestedParallelExecution - true to prevent nested parallel submissions

    • setUseAdaptiveModelParallelism

      public void setUseAdaptiveModelParallelism(boolean useAdaptiveModelParallelism)
      Enable or disable adaptive model-level parallelism.

      When enabled, a ProcessModel execution level with multiple independent areas may run those areas sequentially while preserving child ProcessSystem optimized execution if the children expose substantially more parallel work than the outer area level. This avoids the blunt choice of always using outer area parallelism with child parallelism disabled.

      Parameters:
      useAdaptiveModelParallelism - true to enable adaptive outer-vs-inner parallelism choice

      public void setUseIncrementalAreaExecution(boolean useIncrementalAreaExecution)
      Enable or disable incremental area execution for converging large models.

      When enabled, the first outer iteration runs every area. Later iterations rerun only areas downstream of boundary streams that changed beyond the configured flow, temperature, or pressure tolerances. If lifecycle hooks or event publishing are enabled, all areas are run to preserve callback semantics.

      Parameters:
      useIncrementalAreaExecution - true to allow skipping clean areas in later iterations

      This profile keeps the conservative model-level safeguards enabled, turns on flash warm-start for child ProcessSystems, and applies Wegstein acceleration to all existing Recycle units. The same recycle acceleration is applied to ProcessSystems added after the profile is enabled.

    • setUseFlashWarmStart

      public void setUseFlashWarmStart(boolean useWarmStart)
      Enable or disable flash warm-start K-values for every ProcessSystem in this model.

      When enabled, the iterative TPflash inside every fluid evaluation re-uses the previously converged K-values as the initial estimate instead of seeding from Wilson on every call. This is delegated to ProcessSystem.setUseFlashWarmStart(boolean) on every currently registered ProcessSystem and is also applied to any ProcessSystem added afterwards via add(String, ProcessSystem). Each ProcessSystem manages the underlying ThermodynamicModelSettings flag with try/finally inside its own run() so the setting never leaks past the model run. Default is false (historical behaviour) — recycle-heavy multi-area models are sensitive to flash trajectory and warm-start can shift the converged fixed point.

      Parameters:
      useWarmStart - true to enable warm-start across all ProcessSystems in this model

      public StreamInterface resolveStreamReference(String reference)

      Area-qualified references use "area::streamRef", where streamRef follows ProcessSystem.resolveStreamReference(String) conventions such as feed, separator.gasOut, or splitter.split0. An unqualified reference is accepted only when exactly one process area resolves it.     • runTransient

      public void runTransient(double dt, UUID id)
      Advances every registered ProcessSystem by a single transient step of size dt.

      Areas are stepped in insertion order. Any EventScheduler previously installed via setEventScheduler(EventScheduler) is propagated to each child ProcessSystem before stepping, so a single scheduler can coordinate events across all areas. All area clocks must be finite and aligned before the step; a mismatch fails before any area or shared event state changes.

      Parameters:
      dt - finite timestep size in seconds (must be > 0)
      id - calculation UUID forwarded to each child ProcessSystem.runTransient
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if dt is non-finite or not greater than zero
      IllegalStateException - if child process-area clocks are non-finite or not aligned

    • getTransientTransactionCoverage

      public TransientTransactionCoverage getTransientTransactionCoverage()
      Audits aggregate identity-preserving transient transaction coverage across all process areas.

      Counts are summed over area-local unique process elements. Blocking diagnostics are qualified by area name so duplicate equipment names in different areas remain distinguishable.

      Returns:
      immutable aggregate coverage report

    • beginTransientStepTransaction

      public TransientStepTransaction beginTransientStepTransaction()
      Captures one coordinated rollback point across all process areas.

      Area clocks and complete coverage are validated before the first area transaction is opened. Area transactions are captured in insertion order and rolled back in reverse order, preserving shared boundary-object identities and deterministic replay order.

      Returns:
      open multi-area transaction
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if area clocks are misaligned, coverage is incomplete, or another model transaction is open

    • runTransientTransactional

      public void runTransientTransactional(double dt, UUID id)
      Advances every process area and accepts the common physical step only if all areas succeed.

      A failure in any later area restores already-advanced earlier areas in place. The shared event scheduler bookkeeping is restored with the same object identity by the area transactions.

      Parameters:
      dt - finite timestep in seconds
      id - common physical-step calculation identifier
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if transaction coverage is incomplete

    • run

      public void run()

      - If runStep == true, each process is run in "step" mode exactly once. - Otherwise (continuous mode), it loops up to maxIterations or until all processes are finished (isFinished() == true). If forceIteration is true, the loop runs all maxIterations regardless of convergence.

      When isUseOptimizedExecution() is true (default), each ProcessSystem uses ProcessSystem.runOptimized() for best performance.

      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable

      Runs all ProcessSystems, using parallel execution for independent systems.

      If there are multiple independent ProcessSystems (no shared streams between them), they are executed concurrently using the NeqSim thread pool. Systems that depend on each other are executed sequentially in insertion order.

    • runUntilConverged

      public boolean runUntilConverged(int maxIterations)
      Runs the model until convergence, letting NeqSim work out the flow noise filters by itself.

      This is the recommended entry point for large multi-area plants. It behaves like runUntilConverged(int, double) with the currently configured relative tolerance (default 1e-4, or whatever setTolerance(double) was last given), but with automatic convergence tuning the model no longer needs hand-picked, plant-specific numbers for the boundary flow floor, the absolute flow tolerance, per-section low-flow bypass threshold, or stalled-recycle acceleration.

      After the first outer sweep the total mass flow entering the plant across its feed boundary is measured and every flow-noise threshold is derived from it as a fraction (getAutoTuningFlowFraction(), default 1.0E-6) of that scale. The same model therefore self-configures across scenarios and production years without editing any convergence parameter, and a dead leg carrying a seed flow is recognised as noise rather than dominating the plant-wide relative error. Anything set explicitly by the caller (via setBoundaryFlowFloor(double), setAbsoluteFlowTolerance(double) or a per-unit setMinimumFlow) always wins over the automatic value. A caller choice made with Recycle.setAdaptiveAcceleration(...) likewise takes precedence.

      Call getAutoTuningSummary() afterwards to see the detected flow scale and the thresholds that were applied, or setAutoConvergenceTuning(false) to opt out entirely.

      Parameters:
      maxIterations - maximum number of outer iterations to attempt; must be at least 1
      Returns:
      true if the model converged within the iteration limit, false otherwise
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if maxIterations is less than 1

    • runUntilConverged

      public boolean runUntilConverged(int maxIterations, double tolerance)
      Runs the model in continuous (multi-area) mode until convergence or the iteration limit.

      This is an explicit, agent-friendly convenience wrapper around run(). It guarantees the model runs in iterating mode (not step mode) and applies the supplied iteration limit and tolerance before running. Use this instead of manually configuring setRunStep(boolean), setMaxIterations(int) and setTolerance(double) and hard-coding an outer loop.

      After this call returns, inspect isModelConverged(), getLastIterationCount(), getError() or getConvergenceReportJson() for the outcome.

      Parameters:
      maxIterations - maximum number of outer iterations to attempt; must be at least 1
      tolerance - relative convergence tolerance applied to flow, temperature and pressure; must be a finite positive value
      Returns:
      true if the model converged within the iteration limit, false otherwise
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if maxIterations is less than 1 or tolerance is not a finite positive number

    • runUntilConverged

      public boolean runUntilConverged(int maxIterations, double tolerance, double absoluteFlowTolerance)
      Runs the model until convergence using a combined relative AND absolute flow criterion.

      A boundary stream counts as flow-converged when EITHER its relative flow error is below tolerance OR its absolute flow change is below absoluteFlowTolerance (kg/hr). This is the standard industrial form and is the recommended way to run plants that contain stagnant or nearly-stagnant legs: a stream carrying 0.1 kg/hr can swing 6 % between outer passes (0.007 kg/hr in absolute terms) and would otherwise dominate the relative maximum and mask a genuine multi-hundred kg/hr residual elsewhere in the plant.

      Parameters:
      maxIterations - maximum number of outer iterations to attempt; must be at least 1
      tolerance - relative convergence tolerance applied to flow, temperature and pressure; must be a finite positive value
      absoluteFlowTolerance - absolute flow tolerance in kg/hr; must be finite and non-negative. Use 0.0 for the historical relative-only behaviour
      Returns:
      true if the model converged within the iteration limit, false otherwise
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if maxIterations is less than 1, tolerance is not a finite positive number, or absoluteFlowTolerance is negative or not finite

      public void setBoundaryFlowFloor(double boundaryFlowFloor)
      Sets the flow floor below which a boundary stream is excluded from the convergence metric entirely.

      Streams carrying less than this value are treated as inactive plumbing (a stagnant dead leg, a bypassed section, or a tell-tale seed stream) and neither contribute to the reported maximum errors nor appear in getNonConvergedBoundaryStreamErrors(). The default DEFAULT_BOUNDARY_FLOW_FLOOR excludes only numerically-zero streams; raise it to exclude physically negligible legs as well.

      Parameters:
      boundaryFlowFloor - flow floor in kg/hr; must be finite and non-negative
      Throws:

    • setAutoConvergenceTuning

      public void setAutoConvergenceTuning(boolean autoConvergenceTuning)
      Enables or disables automatic convergence tuning.

      When enabled (the default) the first outer sweep measures the plant's total feed throughput and derives the boundary flow floor, the absolute flow tolerance and - when isAutoLowFlowBypass() is also on - the per-unit low-flow bypass threshold from it. Disabling restores the historical behaviour where every one of those numbers has to be supplied per plant. Values the caller set explicitly are never overridden either way.

      Parameters:
      autoConvergenceTuning - true to let the model tune its own flow-noise filters

    • isAutoLowFlowBypass

    • setAutoLowFlowBypass

      public void setAutoLowFlowBypass(boolean autoLowFlowBypass)
      Enables or disables automatic low-flow bypass of stagnant sections.

      A dead leg (a shut-in injection train, a recompression stage switched off by a split factor) drains towards zero one unit per outer pass and keeps perturbing the convergence gate for tens of iterations. When enabled, units whose inlet flow falls below the detected noise floor are marked inactive for the rest of the run and stop being solved; they reactivate automatically if flow returns. Units with a caller-supplied setMinimumFlow are never touched.

      Parameters:
      autoLowFlowBypass - true to auto-bypass negligible-flow units

    • applyAutoDefaultTolerance

      private void applyAutoDefaultTolerance()
      Applies the engineering-grade default accuracy when the caller did not ask for one.

      The historical default (1e-4 relative on flow, temperature and pressure) is tighter than any process-engineering result needs, and it is what makes recycle-rich plants grind through many extra outer passes. When no tolerance was set explicitly, a plain run() therefore starts from 0.001.

    • relaxToleranceIfStalled

      private boolean relaxToleranceIfStalled()
      Accepts a residual that has stopped improving but is already accurate enough for process work.

      A recycle-rich plant can approach its solution asymptotically: the last decade of the residual costs more outer passes than the whole approach did, and buys an accuracy far below the uncertainty of the fluid model itself. When the worst relative error has not improved materially over 5 outer passes and is still below getAutoToleranceCeiling(), the tolerance is widened to just above that residual and the accepted accuracy is reported through getAutoToleranceSummary(). An explicit tolerance, a residual above the ceiling, or a still-improving residual all suppress this.

      Returns:
      true when the tolerance was widened and convergence must be re-evaluated

    • computeMassClosureError

      private double computeMassClosureError()
      Total mass created or destroyed by open recycle tears, as a fraction of plant feed.

      A recycle whose outlet no longer matches the sum of its inlets is a standing mass source or sink of exactly that difference, so summing the absolute tear imbalances is the mass the flowsheet is failing to conserve. Loops carrying less than the auto-derived boundary floor are skipped as noise.

      Returns:
      relative mass-closure error, or NaN when no usable flow scale exists

    • computeUnitMassClosureError

      private double computeUnitMassClosureError()
      Total mass created or destroyed by non-recycle unit operations, as a fraction of plant feed.

      The recycle-tear figure only covers what the outer solver itself can close. A separator, pipe or mixer whose outlets no longer match its inlets is an equally real mass source or sink, and the boundary residual is blind to it. Bypassed and low-flow units are already excluded by ProcessSystem.getFailedMassBalance(String, double); recycles are skipped here so they are not counted twice.

      Returns:
      relative unit-level closure error, or NaN when no usable flow scale exists

    • getConvergenceReportJson

      public String getConvergenceReportJson()
      Builds a machine-readable JSON convergence report for the last model run.

      This is the structured counterpart to getConvergenceSummary(), intended for agentic workflows that need to parse the convergence outcome rather than read a formatted string. The report is schema-versioned and includes the per-area solved status and the names of any unsolved units, so an agent can pinpoint where a large multi-area model failed to converge.

      Top-level fields: schemaVersion, converged, iterations, maxIterations, boundaryStreamCount, boundaryValuesConverged, allProcessesSolved, maxError, an errors object (flow/temperature/pressure value, tolerance, converged flag and the worstStream that drove the error), a boundaryStreamErrors array naming every boundary stream outside tolerance, and an areas array (one object per process area with name, solved and unsolvedUnits).

      Each boundary stream entry carries name, flowError, temperatureError, pressureError, previousFlowKgPerHr, currentFlowKgPerHr, flowCollapsedToZero and flowStartedFromZero. A relative flow error of exactly 1.0 together with flowCollapsedToZero means the stream stopped flowing between outer passes rather than converging slowly.

      Returns:
      a JSON string describing the convergence outcome of the last run

      public int setMultiPhaseCheck(boolean enabled)
      Enables or disables the multiphase (three-phase) flash on every fluid in every process area of this model.

      Turning the multiphase check off on areas known to be two-phase only avoids the extra phase-stability work in every flash and can speed up the solve considerably. Use setMultiPhaseCheck(String, boolean) to configure a single area, for example to keep the check on in the separation trains but turn it off in the compression and export areas.

    • setPropertyInitLevel

      public int setPropertyInitLevel(Stream.PropertyInitLevel level)
      Sets the physical-property initialization level used by every stream in every process area of this model.

      Selecting Stream.PropertyInitLevel.DENSITY_ONLY skips the viscosity, thermal-conductivity and diffusivity correlations after every stream flash, which is substantially cheaper on a large plant. Use setPropertyInitLevel(String, neqsim.process.equipment.stream.Stream.PropertyInitLevel) to configure a single area, for example to keep full properties in a flow-assurance or heat-exchanger area while running the rest of the plant on mass balances only.

      Warning - transport properties read back as zero under DENSITY_ONLY; see ProcessSystem.setPropertyInitLevel(neqsim.process.equipment.stream.Stream.PropertyInitLevel).

      Parameters:
      level - the level to apply; null restores per-stream control without changing already applied settings
      Returns:
      the total number of distinct streams updated across all areas
      See Also:
      • ProcessSystem.setPropertyInitLevel(neqsim.process.equipment.stream.Stream.PropertyInitLevel)

    • fromJson

      public static ProcessModel fromJson(String json)
      Builds a ProcessModel from a JSON string containing named process areas.

      Expected JSON format: 

      { "areas": { "separation": { "fluid": {...}, "process": [...] }, "compression": {
 "fluid": {...}, "process": [...] } } }

      Each area is built independently using JsonProcessBuilder. If any area fails to build, it is skipped and a warning is logged.

      Parameters:
      json - the JSON string with the "areas" structure
      Returns:
      the built ProcessModel (not yet run)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if JSON is null, empty, or missing the "areas" key
      See Also:
      • toJson()

    • buildFromJson

      public static ProcessModelResult buildFromJson(String json)
      Builds a multi-area ProcessModel from JSON, returning a structured, never-throwing result.

      This is the agent-friendly counterpart to fromJson(String). Where fromJson only logs per-area build failures, this method captures each area's SimulationResult, the names of areas that failed to build, and any inter-area link warnings inside a ProcessModelResult. Invalid input (null, empty, or missing the "areas" key) yields an error result rather than a thrown exception, so an automated pipeline that builds a plant from extracted JSON can degrade gracefully.

      The expected JSON format is identical to fromJson(String): an "areas" object whose values are individual process definitions (as understood by JsonProcessBuilder), plus an optional "interAreaLinks" array.

      Parameters:
      json - the JSON string with the "areas" structure
      Returns:
      a structured build result; never null and never throwing
      See Also:
      • fromJson(String)
      • buildFromJsonAndRun(String)

    • buildFromJsonAndRun

      public static ProcessModelResult buildFromJsonAndRun(String json)
      Builds a multi-area ProcessModel from JSON and runs it, returning a structured, never-throwing result.

      Combines buildFromJson(String) with execution. The model is run only when at least one area built successfully. Run failures are captured as a warning plus the model's run-status JSON instead of being thrown, so an automated pipeline always receives a usable ProcessModelResult.

      Parameters:
      json - the JSON string with the "areas" structure
      Returns:
      a structured build-and-run result; never null and never throwing
      See Also:
      • buildFromJson(String)
      • fromJsonAndRun(String)

    • saveToNeqsim

      public boolean saveToNeqsim(String filename)
      Saves this ProcessModel (with all ProcessSystems) to a compressed .neqsim file.

      This is the recommended format for production use, providing compact storage with full model state preservation including all ProcessSystems. The file can be loaded with loadFromNeqsim(String).

      Example usage: 

       ProcessModel model = new ProcessModel();
 model.add("upstream", upstreamProcess);
 model.add("downstream", downstreamProcess);
 model.run();
 model.saveToNeqsim("multi_process_model.neqsim");
      Parameters:
      filename - the file path to save to (recommended extension: .neqsim)
      Returns:
      true if save was successful, false otherwise

       ProcessModel loaded = ProcessModel.loadFromNeqsim("multi_process_model.neqsim");

 ProcessSystem upstream = loaded.get("upstream");

    • autoSizeEquipment

      public int autoSizeEquipment()
      Auto-sizes all equipment in this model that implements AutoSizeable.

      This method iterates through all process systems in the model and calls autoSize() on each equipment that implements the AutoSizeable interface. The equipment is sized using the default safety factor (1.2 = 20% margin).

      Important: This method should be called AFTER running the process model so that flow rates and conditions are known for sizing calculations.

      Example usage: 

       ProcessModel model = new ProcessModel();
 model.add("upstream", upstreamProcess);
 model.add("downstream", downstreamProcess);
 model.run();
 model.autoSizeEquipment(); // Size all equipment based on actual flow rates
 model.run(); // Re-run with sized equipment
      Returns:
      the number of equipment items that were auto-sized

    • autoSizeEquipment

      public int autoSizeEquipment(double safetyFactor)
      Auto-sizes all equipment in this model with the specified safety factor.

      This method iterates through all process systems in the model and calls autoSize() on each equipment that implements the AutoSizeable interface.

      Parameters:
      safetyFactor - multiplier for design capacity, typically 1.1-1.3 (10-30% over design)
      Returns:
      the number of equipment items that were auto-sized

    • applyMechanicalDesignCapacityConstraints

      public int applyMechanicalDesignCapacityConstraints()
      Applies mechanical-design-derived capacity constraints to every equipment item in every process area of this model.

      This is the multi-area counterpart of ProcessSystem.applyMechanicalDesignCapacityConstraints(). It iterates over all process areas and, for each equipment, derives capacity constraints from the limits configured on its MechanicalDesign. After this call the limits surface in getUtilizationSnapshotJson() (per-area, with area labels) and in each equipment's ProcessEquipmentInterface.getMaxUtilization().

      Typical out-of-the-box workflow for a large multi-area plant: 

       model.run();
 model.autoSizeEquipment(); // populate maxDesign* limits from flow conditions
 model.applyMechanicalDesignCapacityConstraints(); // surface them as utilization
 String snapshot = model.getUtilizationSnapshotJson();

      The method is idempotent and never throws. Call it again whenever design limits or operating conditions change.

      Returns:
      the total number of mechanical-design-derived constraints registered across all areas

    • findBottleneck

      public BottleneckResult findBottleneck()
      Finds the global capacity bottleneck across every process area in this model.

      Each area's most-constrained unit is evaluated via ProcessSystem.findBottleneck() and the unit with the highest utilization across the whole plant is returned. This makes the reservoir / subsurface, midstream and topside areas compete on a single ranking so the true field-wide limiting constraint is surfaced rather than the bottleneck of a single area.

      Returns:
      the plant-wide BottleneckResult; an empty result if no enabled constraints are found in any area

      Checks whether any unit in any area is overloaded (utilization above 100%).

      public Map<String,Double> getCapacityUtilizationSummary()

      Keys use the "area::unit" convention so units with the same name in different areas do not collide. Values are maximum constraint utilization in percent.

    • enableAllConstraints

      public int enableAllConstraints()
      Enables all capacity constraints on every unit in every area of this model.

      This is the plant-wide preset that switches subsurface, midstream and topside constraints on in one call, mirroring ProcessSystem.enableAllConstraints() at the multi-area level.

      Returns:
      the total number of constraints enabled across all areas

    • getUtilizationSnapshotJson

      public String getUtilizationSnapshotJson()
      Returns a stable, side-effect-free JSON utilization snapshot of every unit across all process areas in this plant.

      This is the multi-area counterpart of ProcessSystem.getUtilizationSnapshotJson() and the recommended observation endpoint for machine-learning / reinforcement-learning optimization loops on a full plant. Each unit entry carries an "area" property. A non-null plant-wide bottleneck carries both "area" and the unambiguous "qualifiedName" ("area::unit"), in addition to its legacy "name". The anyOverloaded and anyHardLimitExceeded flags summarise the whole model. Schema is versioned by schemaVersion ("1.0").

      The method does not run the model; call run() (or ProcessAutomation.evaluate(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Double>, java.lang.String, java.util.List<java.lang.String>, java.lang.String, int, double)) first so the reported utilization reflects the latest setpoints.

      Returns:
      JSON string {schemaVersion, name, units:[...], bottleneck:{...}, anyOverloaded, anyHardLimitExceeded}

    • getAutomation

      public ProcessAutomation getAutomation()
      Returns an automation facade for this process model. The facade provides a stable, string-addressable API for scripts and AI agents to interact with all process areas using area-qualified addresses like "AreaName::UnitName.property".

      The facade is cached and reused across calls so that diagnostics (learned corrections, operation history, dirty-state tracking) persist for the lifetime of the process model.

      Returns:
      a ProcessAutomation facade
